messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: svc-auth 5xx surge in eu-west-1 (impact: session creation failures). Incident ID INC-2025298765432. Primary: Maya. Auto-assigning bridge.

OpsBot: Bridge created -> https://meet.example.com/bridge/INC-2025298765432. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/svc-auth 

Maya: hey team — I'm on a train, stuck in a tunnel, ETA ~45m. I'm the primary for this shift but can't reliably be on the bridge for the first hour. Sorry for the last-minute callout.

Sam: I can be primary for the first 60m. Taking the bridge now. @Maya -- do you want me to continue if still on the train after that?

Maya: yes please, Sam. pls follow runbook priority 1 and target the fallback path. I'll shadow async and pick up once i'm off the train. Thanks 🙏

Jon: I'll be secondary and monitor alerts + customer slack. If we need capacity scaling I can trigger the Dedicated burst for eu-west-1.

Priya: quick note on impact — I see ~12% session creation failures from 04:22 UTC, spike correlates with deploy at 04:18 but rollout status looks green. Could be worker OOM or KV throttling.

Sam: good call. Starting with the runbook checklist. Step 1: confirm error type. Logs show 502 gateway from auth-worker.

Sam: running the quick mitigation from runbook: prefix cache bypass and restart one worker pool. Command:```bash
# restart worker pool with drain
redwoodctl worker restart --service svc-auth --pool auth-pool-2 --grace 30s
```

Jon: copying the log snippet I saw:```json
{"ts":"2025-11-12T04:23:09Z","service":"auth-worker","err":"malloc failed","pid":1245}
```

Priya: malloc failed suggests memory pressure. If restart doesn't help, switch traffic to auth-pool-1 and pin a lighter quantized model variant for auth-checks. Runbook section: "Emergency fallback: traffic split to warm pool" -> https://go/runbooks/svc-auth#fallback

Sam: restarted auth-pool-2, drain complete. Monitoring... :eyes:

OpsBot: Notice: scaled up auth-pool-1 by +2 instances (policy: manual-scale) per Sam's request.

Maya: thanks Sam & Jon. I'm tagging out for now until I can join properly. Please follow the handoff steps in the oncall doc: https://go/oncall-handoffs.

Sam: taking primary formally. I'll annotate in pager-duty. Current customer impact: session failures reduced to ~3% after restart. Will keep bridge open for 30m. :thumbsup:

Jon: I'm monitoring downstream services and the status page. If it stays under 5% for 20m we can move to mitigation review and close incident.

Priya: adding postmortem checklist item: verify memory regression for latest image, include heap profiles from 04:00-04:30.

Maya: lingering ask — if you need me to run any KV flush commands once i'm back, ping and I'll do it. Good handoff. :heart:

Sam: noted. I'll leave a short runbook note in the incident doc with the exact commands I ran.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2025298765432 status update: mitigated -> degraded -> monitoring. Assigned: Sam (primary), Jon (secondary).

Jon: leaving the bridge in 20m but will stay on pager for the remainder of my shift. If anyone else can cover after Sam signs off, please claim and call out in this thread.

Sam: will update here when we hit stable 20m window. For any follow-ups: key commands, logs, and links are in the incident doc: https://go/incidents/INC-2025298765432.

Maya: huge thanks to everyone for the quick cover. I owe coffee next week :coffee:

Sam: :coffee: accepted. Closing the on-bridge primary handoff notes now.

OpsBot: Reminder: please run the post-incident checklist and tag the PM + Security for review.

Priya: noted, I'll start a minimal postmortem draft and include heap dumps + regressed image.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2025298765432 updated: last_event_ts=5298765459, work_notes_added_by=Sam.

Sam: final status — stable 32m, moving to postmortem. If no objections, I'll hand back primary to Maya when she's online. :rocket:

Maya: back online in 40m, will take primary then. Thanks all.
